steps.title: Prepare Vero‑E6 Complete Growth Medium
steps.instruction: Combine DMEM (High Glucose) with 1 % P/S (10 000 U/mL), 1 % MEM NEAA, 10 % FBS, and 10 mM HEPES to a final volume of 500 mL; store at 4 °C (≤6 weeks) and warm to 37 °C before use.

steps.title: Prepare Vero‑E6 Complete Infection Medium
steps.instruction: Mix DMEM (High Glucose) with 1 % P/S (10 000 U/mL) and 2 % FBS to a final volume of 500 mL; store at 4 °C (≤6 weeks) and warm to 37 °C before use.

steps.title: Make 1 % Agarose Solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g SeaKem ME agarose in 100 mL boiling Milli‑Q water, autoclave, then keep at 20‑22 °C; melt before use and keep at 55 °C in a water bath.

steps.title: Prepare EMEM + 14 % FBS Medium
steps.instruction: Combine EMEM 2× with 14 % FBS and 2 % GlutaMAX (200 mM) to a final volume of 500 mL; store at 4 °C (≤6 weeks) and bring to 20‑22 °C before use.

steps.title: Prepare Plaque Assay Overlay Medium
steps.instruction: Equilibrate EMEM + 14 % FBS at 20‑22 °C; immediately before overlay mix equal volumes of this medium and 1 % agarose (kept at 55 °C) to obtain a 0.5 % agarose overlay (total 100 mL). Use immediately.

steps.title: Prepare 25 % Formaldehyde Solution
steps.instruction: Mix 33.8 mL 37 % formaldehyde with 16.2 mL PBS 1× to obtain 50 mL of 25 % formaldehyde; store at 4 °C (≤1 week) and dispose of safely.

steps.title: Prepare 1 % Crystal Violet Stain
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g crystal violet in 20 mL absolute ethanol, add 25 mL 37 % formaldehyde and 55 mL PBS 1× to make 100 mL of 1 % crystal violet solution; store at 20‑22 °C protected from light (≤4 months) and mix before each use.

steps.title: Prepare Complete E8 Medium for hPSC
steps.instruction: Combine 485 mL E8 basal medium, 10 mL E8 supplement (50×), and 5 mL P/S (10 000 U/mL) to a total of 500 mL; store at 4 °C (≤2 weeks), warm only the required amount to 20‑22 °C (never 37 °C) and protect from light.

steps.title: Make CHIR Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 125 mg CHIR in DMSO to a final volume of 896 µL (≈128 µM); aliquot 50 µL and store at –20 °C (≤6 months).

steps.title: Make Activin A Stock (50 µg/mL)
steps.instruction: Dilute Activin A to 50 µg/mL using sterile 4 mM HCl; total volume 1 000 µL (500 µg); aliquot 20‑50 µL and store at –20 °C (≤6 months), avoiding repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Make FGF9 Stock (50 µg/mL)
steps.instruction: Dilute recombinant human FGF9 to 50 µg/mL with distilled cell‑culture grade water; total volume 10 000 µL (500 µg); aliquot 100 µL and store at –20 °C (≤6 months), avoiding repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Make Heparin Stock (50 mg/mL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve heparin to 50 mg/mL in distilled cell‑culture grade water; total volume 1 000 µL (50 mg); aliquot 50 µL and store at 4 °C (≤2 years). Prepare an intermediate 5 mg/mL stock by diluting 1:10 when needed.

steps.title: Prepare Advanced RPMI Complete Medium
steps.instruction: Combine 49 mL Advanced RPMI 1640 basal medium, 10.5 mL P/S (10 000 U/mL), and 10.5 mL GlutaMAX (200 mM) to a final volume of 500 mL; store at 4 °C (≤4 weeks) and bring to 20‑22 °C before use.

steps.title: Prepare Posterior Primitive Streak Medium
steps.instruction: To 15 mL of Complete Advanced RPMI, add 10 µL CHIR (12 mM) to achieve 8 µM final; bring to 20‑22 °C before use.

steps.title: Prepare Intermediate Mesoderm Induction Medium
steps.instruction: To 15 mL of Complete Advanced RPMI, add 60 µL FGF9 (50 µg/mL) for 200 ng/mL, 3 µL Activin A (50 µg/mL) for 10 ng/mL, and 3 µL Heparin (5 mg/mL) for 1 µg/mL (use intermediate 5 mg/mL heparin stock); bring to 20‑22 °C before use.

steps.title: Prepare CHIR‑Pulse Organoid Induction Medium
steps.instruction: To 15 mL of Complete Advanced RPMI, add 60 µL FGF9 (50 µg/mL) for 200 ng/mL, 3 µL Heparin (5 mg/mL) for 1 µg/mL, and 6.25 µL CHIR (12 mM) for 5 µM; use intermediate 5 mg/mL heparin stock; bring to 20‑22 °C before use.

steps.title: Prepare Kidney Organoid Differentiation Medium
steps.instruction: To 40 mL of Complete Advanced RPMI, add 160 µL FGF9 (50 µg/mL) for 200 ng/mL and 8 µL Heparin (5 mg/mL) for 1 µg/mL (use intermediate 5 mg/mL heparin stock); bring to 20‑22 °C before use.

steps.title: Make 1 M D‑Glucose Stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 18.0 g D‑glucose in 80 mL distilled water, stir until dissolved, bring to 100 mL with water, filter through 0.22 µm syringe filter, store at 4 °C (≤2 months); do not autoclave.

steps.title: Make 1 M D‑Mannitol Stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve 18.2 g D‑mannitol in 80 mL distilled water, stir until dissolved, bring to 100 mL with water, filter through 0.22 µm syringe filter, store at 20‑22 °C (≤2 months) to avoid crystal formation.

steps.title: Prepare Normoglycemic Medium (5 mM Glucose)
steps.instruction: Combine 477.5 mL glucose‑free DMEM, 5 % P/S, 5 % GlutaMAX, 2.5 mL 1 M D‑glucose (final 5 mM), and 10 mL 1 M D‑mannitol (final 20 mM) to 500 mL; store at 4 °C (≤6 weeks) and warm to 37 °C before use.

steps.title: Prepare Hyperglycemic Medium (25 mM Glucose)
steps.instruction: Combine 477.5 mL glucose‑free DMEM, 5 % P/S, 5 % GlutaMAX, and 12.5 mL 1 M D‑glucose (final 25 mM) to 500 mL; store at 4 °C (≤6 weeks) and warm to 37 °C before use.

steps.title: Prepare 4 % PFA Fixative
steps.instruction: Mix 12.5 mL 16 % PFA with 37.5 mL PBS 1× to obtain 50 mL of 4 % PFA; store at 4 °C (≤1 week) and dispose of safely.

steps.title: Prepare 10× TBS (pH 7.6)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 24 g Trizma base and 88 g NaCl in 900 mL Milli‑Q water, adjust pH to 7.6 with HCl, then bring to 1 000 mL; store at 4 °C (≤6 months).

steps.title: Prepare 1× TBS (pH 7.6)
steps.instruction: Dilute 100 mL of 10× TBS with 900 mL distilled water to 1 000 mL; store at 4 °C (≤6 months).

steps.title: Prepare TBS + 1 % Triton X‑100
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL Triton X‑100 to 100 mL 1× TBS to obtain 1 % Triton; store at 4 °C (≤2 weeks).

steps.title: Prepare TBS + 0.5 % Triton X‑100
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 mL Triton X‑100 to 100 mL 1× TBS to obtain 0.5 % Triton; store at 4 °C (≤2 weeks).

steps.title: Prepare Whole‑Mount Blocking Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 9.4 mL TBS + 1 % Triton X‑100 with 600 µL donkey serum (6 % final) to 10 mL; filter through 0.22 µm syringe filter and store at 4 °C (≤1 week).

steps.title: Prepare Paraffin‑Section Blocking Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 9.7 mL TBS + 1 % Triton X‑100 with 300 µL donkey serum (3 % final) to 1 000 µL; filter through 0.22 µm syringe filter and store at 4 °C (≤1 week).

steps.title: Prepare TBS + 1 % Triton + 1 % BSA
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 g BSA to 50 mL TBS + 1 % Triton X‑100 to obtain 1 % BSA; filter through 0.22 µm syringe filter and store at 4 °C (≤1 week).

steps.title: Prepare TBS + 0.5 % Triton + 1 % BSA
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 g BSA to 50 mL TBS + 0.5 % Triton X‑100 to obtain 1 % BSA; filter through 0.22 µm syringe filter and store at 4 °C (≤1 week).

steps.title: Dilute Primary Antibodies
steps.instruction: Dilute ACE2 1:20, NP 1:500, and LTL 1:200 in TBS + 1 % Triton + 1 % BSA for whole‑mount or in TBS + 0.5 % Triton + 1 % BSA for paraffin sections; prepare fresh.

steps.title: Dilute Secondary Antibodies
steps.instruction: Dilute anti‑goat‑AF488 1:200, anti‑mouse‑Cy3 1:200, and streptavidin‑Dylight 649 1:40 in the same buffers used for the corresponding primary antibodies; prepare fresh.

steps.title: Prepare DAPI Stock Solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mg DAPI in 2 mL distilled water to obtain 5 mg/mL (14.3 mM); aliquot 20‑50 µL and store at –20 °C in the dark (≤6 months), avoiding repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Prepare DAPI Working Solution (1:5000)
steps.instruction: Dilute 1 µg/mL DAPI (from stock) in 10 mL TBS 1× to make 10 mL of 1:5000 working solution; prepare fresh and dispose of safely.

steps.title: Produce SARS‑CoV‑2 Virus Stock
steps.instruction: Grow Vero‑E6 cells to 90 % confluence in ten 75‑cm² flasks (6.5‑9.5 × 10⁴ cells/cm²) in Complete Growth Medium; seed two additional flasks for mock control and cell counting; incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂. The next day count cells, calculate virus volume for MOI 0.01 using the formula (cells × MOI)/titer, e.g., ~6.5 µL per flask for a 10⁷ PFU/mL stock. Thaw seed stock at 20‑22 °C, dilute in DMEM + 2 % FBS (Complete Infection Medium), and inoculate each flask: remove medium, wash once with 3 mL PBS, add 3 mL virus‑containing Complete Infection Medium (or fresh medium for mock), incubate 1 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, then add 7 mL Complete Growth Medium. Monitor daily for CPE (48‑72 h). When ~90 % CPE is observed, collect supernatant into sterile 15 mL tubes, discard cells, centrifuge 450 × g 5 min at 4 °C, aliquot 200‑500 µL into labeled 2 mL screw‑caps, and store at –80 °C, minimizing freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Allocate Fixed Organoids for IF
steps.instruction: After fixing kidney organoids with 4 % PFA (step 30), divide the specimens as desired for whole‑mount immunofluorescence or for paraffin‑section immunofluorescence.

description: The protocol herein outlines the detailed procedures for using SARS-CoV-2 virus isolates to infect human kidney organoids. Specifically, we describe the steps to prepare SARS-CoV-2 virus stocks and determine virus titers using Vero-E6 Cells. We also detail the methodology to culture and differentiate hPSC into kidney organoids, and how to induce diabetic-like kidney organoids in vitro. Next, we explain how to efficiently infect human kidney organoids with SARS-CoV-2 and assess infection by immunofluorescence and confocal imaging.CRITICAL: All laboratory procedures related to virus preparation, infection of cell cultures/organoids or collection of infected cells/organoids must be performed in certified class II biological safety cabinets in a Biosafety Level 3 (BSL-3) containment laboratory. Personnel are required to wear appropriate personal protective equipment to protect from biological risks as determined by local requirements. Personal equipment as well as virus handling and decontamination of all materials must be performed before exiting the containment area. This includes decontamination of all tubes/samples that exit the BSL-3 area as well as ensuring that all protocols to collect RNA and protein are shown to kill any infectious virus. The protocols that state whether a virus has been inactivated must be tested, reviewed and approved by the competent Institutional Biosafety Committees or National agencies depending on the requirements at your institution.
